answer_1.quote: We propose the Counterfactual Recipe Generation task, to examine models' compositional generalization ability in understanding and generating recipe texts. ... We finetune pretrained language models (PLMs) on our collected Chinese recipe corpus to learn culinary knowledge, and use prevalent unsupervised counterfactual generation frameworks to generate counterfactual recipes ...

answer_2.quote: We first evaluate the generated texts from two aspects, to answer the L1 question: ... Coverage of Ingredients. ... Extent of Preservation. We calculate the correspondence between the generated recipe and the base recipe with BLEU and BERTScore. ... We measure the precision, recall, and F1 score between the changes, C, made by a model and the pivot actions, P.

answer_4.quote: We conduct a human evaluation to assess model performance more comprehensively ... we ask raters to choose the best and worst generated recipes on grammaticality (whether the text is grammatically correct and fluent), correctness (whether the text is a correct recipe of the target dish), and preservation (whether the text preserves the base recipe's cooking and writing style).
answer_4.guideline: Raters select the best and worst recipes for each instance based on three questions: grammaticality, correctness, and preservation.
